extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (including pro se applicants), patent agents/attorneys, and examiners preparing U.S. utility patent application specifications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the preferred arrangement, section headings, formatting, and substantive content of a U.S. utility patent application specification (per MPEP §608.01(a)). Covers required sections, formatting rules, file incorporation, and special requirements like sequence listings, claims, and abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of application elements (37 C.F.R. 1.77(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The elements of the application, if applicable, should appear in the following order: (1) Utility application transmittal form; (2) Fee transmittal form; (3) Application data sheet (§ 1.76); (4) Specification; (5) Drawings; (6) The inventor’s oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the preferred order for the filing packet. Use when assembling the filing to promote correct processing by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of specification sections (37 C.F.R. 1.77(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification should include the following sections in order: (1) Title of the invention; (2) Cross-reference to related applications; (3) Statement regarding federally sponsored research or development; (4) The names of the parties to a joint research agreement; (5) Incorporation by reference statement for certain electronic file types; (6) Statement regarding prior disclosures by the inventor(s); (7) Background of the invention; (8) Brief summary of the invention; (9) Brief description of the several views of the drawing; (10) Detailed description of the invention; (11) A claim or claims; (12) Abstract of the disclosure; (13) Sequence Listing (where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ordering is the preferred arrangement for a nonprovisional specification. Each item should be present as applicable; sequence listing requirements (item 13) are addressed in 37 C.F.R. 1.821–1.825 and MPEP §§ 2421–2431.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section heading formatting and 'Not Applicable' convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of the specification sections defined in paragraphs (b)(1) through (b)(12), if applicable, should be preceded by a section heading in uppercase and without underlining or bold type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no text follows a section heading, the phrase "Not Applicable" should follow the section heading. Section headings should appear in uppercase, without underlining or bold. This formatting is recommended for clarity and uniformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference versus requirement for arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: The order of arrangement of specification elements as set forth in 37 CFR 1.77(b) is preferable (e.g., not required) in framing the nonprovisional specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the order is preferred, deviations are not strictly prohibited; however, following the preferred order facilitates examination and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) control and discrepancies
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76) is used, data supplied in the application data sheet need not be provided elsewhere in the application. For applications filed on or after Sept. 16, 2012, if there is a discrepancy between information in an ADS and elsewhere in the application, the ADS will control except for naming of inventors (governed by 37 CFR 1.41). The most recent compliant ADS governs foreign priority or domestic benefit claims (37 CFR 1.76(d)). For pre-Sept. 16, 2012 applications, ADS controls except for naming inventors and citizenship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the ADS is accurate and up-to-date; naming and inventorship changes are governed by other rules (e.g., 37 CFR 1.48).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form Paragraphs for pro se applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant (typically a pro se) may be advised of the proper arrangement by using Form Paragraph 6.01 or 6.02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 6.01 (Arrangement of the Sections of the Specification) and 6.02 (Content of Specification) illustrate preferred layout and content and are suggested for advising pro se filers.

rubrics_metrics.name: TITLE OF THE INVENTION content and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention should be placed at the top of the first page of the specification unless the title is provided in an application data sheet. The title should be brief but technically accurate and descriptive, preferably from two to seven words. It may not contain more than 500 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the title concise and technically descriptive. If using an ADS, the title may be supplied there; otherwise place it at the top of the specification's first page.

rubrics_metrics.name: CROSS-REFERENCES TO RELATED APPLICATIONS
rubrics_metrics.description: Include cross-references to related applications as appropriate (see 37 CFR 1.78 and MPEP §211 et seq.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow statutory/regulatory rules for claiming priority/benefit; include serial/app numbers, filing dates, and jurisdictions as required by cited rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: STATEMENT REGARDING FEDERALLY SPONSORED RESEARCH OR DEVELOPMENT
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a statement regarding federally sponsored research or development where applicable (see MPEP §310).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose federal sponsorship if the invention was made with federal support, following regulatory mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: NAMES OF THE PARTIES TO A JOINT RESEARCH AGREEMENT
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the names of the parties to a joint research agreement when applicable (see 37 CFR 1.71(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide required information about joint research agreement parties to address potential joint inventorship and rights issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation-by-reference of electronic material (read-only discs, text files, XML)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification is required to include an incorporation-by-reference of electronic documents that are to become part of the permanent USPTO records. For ASCII plain text files submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system or on read-only optical discs, identify the names of each file, the date of creation of each file, and the size of each file in bytes for document types such as: (A) Computer Program Listing Appendix (§ 1.96(c)); (B) Sequence Listing (§ 1.821(c)); (C) Large Tables (§ 1.58(c)). Also applies to an XML file for a "Sequence Listing XML" (§ 1.831(a)) submitted via PES or on read-only optical discs, identifying names/date/size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When incorporating electronic materials, explicitly identify each file and its metadata (name, creation date, byte size) so the files become part of the application record. See MPEP §608.05 and USPTO Legal Framework for Patent Electronic System for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: STATEMENT REGARDING PRIOR DISCLOSURES BY THE INVENTOR
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a statement regarding prior disclosures by the inventor or a joint inventor (see 35 U.S.C. 102(b) and 37 CFR 1.77).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose any prior public disclosures made by the inventor(s); this addresses statutory bars and prior art issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION: Field and Related Art
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification should set forth the Background of the Invention in two parts: (1) Field of the Invention — a statement of the field of art, may paraphrase applicable U.S. patent classification definitions; (2) Description of Related Art — description of related art known to the applicant, including references to specific related art and problems in the prior art which are solved by the applicant’s invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background may be titled "Technical Field" and "Background Art." Include relevant prior art references and state problems solved to contextualize the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief summary or general statement of the invention as set forth in 37 CFR 1.73. The summary is separate and distinct from the abstract and is directed toward the invention rather than the disclosure as a whole. The summary may point out advantages of the invention or how it solves prior art problems and in chemical cases should point out the utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set forth the nature and gist of the inventive concept if possible; treat objects of the invention briefly and only to the extent they help understanding. Do not substitute the abstract for the summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE SEVERAL VIEWS OF THE DRAWING(S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a reference to and brief description of the drawing(s) as set forth in 37 CFR 1.74.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concise descriptions of each figure/view so that the drawings are clear and referenced in the detailed description.

rubrics_metrics.name: DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION (preferred embodiments)
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of the preferred embodiment(s) as required in 37 CFR 1.71. The description should be as short and specific as is necessary to describe the invention adequately and accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not describe conventional, widely known elements in unnecessary detail if their exact nature is not needed for a person skilled in the art to practice the invention. For particularly complicated subject matter or unfamiliar elements, refer to another patent or readily available publication that adequately describes them.

rubrics_metrics.name: CLAIM OR CLAIMS formatting and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim or claims must commence on a separate sheet or electronic page (37 CFR 1.52(b)(3)). Where a claim sets forth a plurality of elements or steps, each element or step of the claim should be separated by a line indentation. There may be plural indentations to further segregate subcombinations or related steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place claims on a separate sheet/page and format with line indentations between elements or steps to clearly delineate claim structure. See 37 CFR 1.75 and MPEP 608.01(i)-(p) for further claim formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: ABSTRACT OF THE DISCLOSURE requirements and length
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract is a brief narrative of the disclosure as a whole, in a single paragraph preferably not exceeding 150 words, commencing on a separate sheet following the claims. In an international application entering the national stage, an abstract published with the international application may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the abstract concise (preferably ≤150 words) and present it on a separate sheet. The USPTO will use the abstract published by WIPO if applicable for national-stage filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEQUENCE LISTING requirement and submission formats
rubrics_metrics.description: A "Sequence Listing" is required by 37 CFR 1.821–1.825 and MPEP §§ 2421–2431 for any nucleotide or amino acid sequence disclosed in an application; the requirement applies to all sequences disclosed whether claimed or not. A sequence listing may be submitted as a PDF, as an ASCII text file via PES or on read-only optical disc, or as an XML file for a "Sequence Listing XML" (see § 1.831(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the required sequence listing is not submitted electronically, it must be submitted on paper. Ensure compliance with file-type, metadata (file name/date/size), and submission-route requirements to avoid defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended that provisional applications follow the same general format as the nonprovisional specification, although claims are not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although provisional filings do not require claims, adopting the recommended arrangement increases clarity and may ease conversion or continuity filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim indentation and subcombination formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claim sets forth a plurality of elements or steps, each element or step should be separated by a line indentation; there may be plural indentations to further segregate subcombinations or related steps (see 37 CFR 1.75).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use indentation consistently to show claim element hierarchy and subcombinations for readability and correct claim interpretation.
